Rashi on Niddah 55b:11:1.hebrew: במה שביד טהור - אם רק במה שביד טהור, דהוה ליה טהור נושא את הרוק:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:11:1.english: In that which is in the hand of a pure person - If [the zav] spat onto that which is in the hand of a pure person, for the pure person is [thereby] carrying the saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:13:1.hebrew: זה מגע נבלה - שטהרתי לך בגדים שעליו, וטמאתים לך כאן במגע הרוק:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:13:1.english: This is contact with an animal carcass - Where I deemed pure for you the garments upon him, and I deemed them impure for you here upon contact with the saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:1.hebrew: ואימא משא דשרץ - שטהרתי לך את הנושאו, טמאתי לך בכאן בנושא הרוק, אבל מגעו כנבלה:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:1.english: And say: The carrying of a creeping animal - That [whereas] I declared pure for you the one who carries it, I declared [him] impure for you here in the case of the one who carries saliva; but contact with it [should be] like [contact with] a carcass.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:2.hebrew: לימא באדם - דדרשינן במה שביד אדם, והיינו משאו, ובלאו דרשא דטהרה שטהרתי לך וכו' נפקא לן משא:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:2.english: Let it say: "On a person" - For we would expound: [Into] that which is in the hand of a person, and this is carrying it; and without the exposition of "a purity that I deemed pure for you, etc.," carrying is derived for us.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:3.hebrew: מאי בטהור - דמשמע טהרה שטהרתי במקום אחר, טמאתי בכאן:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:3.english: What is [the meaning of] "on the pure person"? - For it implies: "A purity that I declared pure in another place, I have declared impure here."

Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:4.hebrew: ש"מ תרתי - משא מרבויא דבי"ת שבטהור, ומגע לטמא בגדים מטהור:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:14:4.english: Conclude two [things] from it - Carrying [is derived] from the inclusion of the [letter] *beit* in "ba-tahor," and [that] contact defiles garments [is derived] from "tahor."

Rashi on Niddah 55b:15:1.english: In [the case of fluids] drawn through the mouth - That he drew them and brought them out through the mouth.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:15:2.hebrew: ורחמנא רבייה - מכי ירוק, כל דדמי לרוק:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:15:2.english: And the Merciful One included it - From [the verse] "And if he spits," [to include] anything that is similar to saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:1.hebrew: ורב - כיון דלאו מעין הוא, אלא מפני שגררן דרך פיו קתני לה, ומשום צחצוחי הרוק:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:1.english: And Rav - Since [nasal fluids] are not a [primary] secretion, but rather [the tanna] taught it [only] because he drew them through his mouth, and on account of the traces of saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:2.hebrew: ליחשוב נמי - במתניתא דמעת עינו, ונוקמה בשגוררה דרך הפה, דהאמר רב: אפשר לגוררה דרך הפה:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:2.english: Let it also count - In the baraita, the tear of his eye, and let us establish it [as referring to a case] where he dragged it through the mouth, as Rav said: It is possible to drag it through the mouth.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:3.english: For Rav said: One who desires to become blind - That he should become blind.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:4.hebrew: ליכחול עיניה מעובד כוכבים ולוי אמר כו' - מאי טעמא דרב דלא אמר לימות? דסבר: אם נתן העובד כוכבים לתוכו סם המות, יכול לגוררו ולהוציאו דרך פיו, כדרך הרוקקין שמושכין מי האף בפיהם ע"י רוח נשימתם לגופן:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:16:4.english: Should have a gentile paint his eye, and Levi said, etc. - What is Rav's reason that he did not say 'he will die'? For he holds: If the gentile placed poison into it, he can draw it and bring it out through his mouth, in the manner of those who spit, who draw nasal fluid into their mouth by means of the breath of their inhalation into their body.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:17:1.english: The poison - The venom of a deadly poison.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:18:1.english: Foul secretion - Cuiture in Old French [meaning pus].

Rashi on Niddah 55b:18:3.english: The ritual impurity of liquids - To render foods and liquids impure, like other impure liquids.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:18:4.english: With a quarter-log - This is the [standard] measure of liquids for ritual impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:18:5.hebrew: טומאה חמורה - אדם ובגדים, דמעיינות הן:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:18:5.english: Severe impurity - [To defile] a person and garments, for they are bodily emanations [ma'ayanot].

Rashi on Niddah 55b:19:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב - דאמר האי דקתני להו תנא דלעיל בנגררין דרך הפה, איכא לתרוצי דהאי תנא להכי לא תני להו: דכיון דטומאתן לאו מחמת עצמן היא אלא משום צחצוחי רוק, לא פסיקא ליה, דהא זימנין דנפקי דרך חוטם וטהורין, ובמילתא דלא פסיקא לא קמיירי:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:19:1.english: Granted, according to Rav - Who said that that which the Tanna above taught [regarding them is when they are] drawn out through the mouth, one can explain that this Tanna did not teach them for this reason: Since their impurity is not due to themselves, but rather because of traces of saliva, it is not categorical to him [to include them], for sometimes they emerge through the nose and are pure, and he does not deal with a matter that is not categorical.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:19:2.hebrew: אלא לרבי יוחנן - דאמר לעולם טמאין, ליתני:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:19:2.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan - Who said [that they are] always impure, let [the tanna] teach [them].

Rashi on Niddah 55b:1:1.hebrew: נבלה - במגע מטמאה אדם ולא בגדים שעליו, ובמשא מטמאה אדם ובגדים שעליו, כדכתיב (ויקרא י״א:כ״ז-כ״ח): והנוגע בנבלתה יטמא עד הערב, והנושא את נבלתה יכבס בגדיו, אבל במגע לא כתיב כבוס. זב, אפילו מגעו מטמא בגדים, דכתיב: והנוגע בבשר הזב יכבס בגדיו; וכן משאו, דכתיב במשכב ומושב: והנושא אותם יכבס בגדיו, וקל וחומר לנושא זב עצמו:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:1:1.english: An animal carcass - Through contact, it transmits impurity to a person but not to the garments upon him, and through carrying, it transmits impurity to a person and to the garments upon him, as it is written (Leviticus 11:27–28): "And whoever touches its carcass shall be impure until evening," and "And he who carries its carcass shall wash his garments"—but regarding contact, washing [of garments] is not written. [Regarding a] zav, even contact with him transmits impurity to garments, as it is written: "And whoever touches the flesh of the zav shall wash his garments" (Leviticus 15:7); and so too carrying him, as it is written regarding a bed and a seat: "And whoever carries them shall wash his garments" (Leviticus 15:10), and an a fortiori argument applies to one who carries the zav himself.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:21:1.english: And You gave them tears to drink in great measure - Evidently, [tears] are called a liquid.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:21:2.hebrew: דם חללים ישתה - אלמא דם חלל איקרי משקה, ודם מגפתו נמי דם חללים הוא, דהא קטליה פלגיה:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:21:2.english: He shall drink the blood of the slain - Evidently, the blood of a slain person is called a liquid, and the blood of his wound is also [considered] blood of the slain, for he has killed part of him.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:22:1.hebrew: זובו טמא וזאת - דסמיך ליה: "וזאת תהיה טומאתו" וגו', ודרשי האי "וזאת" אקרא דלעיל: "זובו טמא וזאת", כלומר: דבר אחר נמי כזוב:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:22:1.english: His issue is impure, and this - For juxtaposed to it is: "And this shall be his impurity..." etc., and they expound this "and this" [in connection] with the preceding verse: "His issue is impure, and this" — that is to say, another thing is also like [his] issue.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:3:1.hebrew: והשתא דנפקא לן - טומאת הזב מוהזב את זובו, דאיתקש זובו לו, זובו טמא למה לי:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:3:1.english: And now that we derive - The impurity of the zav from "and of one who emits his issue," as his issue is juxtaposed to him, why do I need "his issue is impure"?

Rashi on Niddah 55b:5:1.hebrew: זב חדא זובו תרתי - וכתיב לזכר, דבשתי ראיות ראשונות דין זכר עליו, שאינו מטמא באונס; ומכאן ואילך איתקש לנקבה, דאפילו ראה שלישי באונס חייב קרבן:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:5:1.english: "Zav" [indicates] one, "his issue" [indicates] two - And it is written, "For the male" — that for the first two emissions the law of a male applies to him, that he does not become ritually impure due to an accident; and from here on, he is juxtaposed to a female, so that even if he saw a third [emission] due to an accident, he is obligated to bring an offering.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:6:1.hebrew: והשתא דכתיב זובו טמא - דנפקא לן מיניה עיקר טומאת זוב, מהשתא דרוש מוהזב את זובו הך דרשא דלא תחלוק בין מגעו למשאו, ואע"פ שאתה דורשו לדרשא אחריני:
Rashi on Niddah 55b:6:1.english: And now that it is written: "His issue is impure" - Since we derive from it the fundamental impurity of the discharge, now expound from "and of one who emits his issue" this derivation, that you shall not distinguish between contact with it and carrying it, even though you [also] expound it for another derivation.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:8:1.english: His phlegm and his mucus - They are a type of saliva.

Rashi on Niddah 55b:8:2.english: The verse states: "And if he spits" - [The Tanna] expounds the letter vav.

Tosafot on Niddah 55b:10:1.hebrew: נילף רוק רוק מיבמה - תימה, דהשתא נילף רוק דיבמה מהכא דנגע! ויש לומר, דבסיפרי דרשינן ליה מקרא דלא בעינן נגע: "וירקה בפניו" — יכול בפניו ממש? ת"ל "לעיני הזקנים" — רוק הנראה לזקנים:
Tosafot on Niddah 55b:10:1.english: Let us derive "spit" "spit" from a yevama - It is astonishing: for now, let us derive the spit of a yevama from here, that it [must] touch! And one can say that in the Sifrei we derive from a verse that we do not require [it to] touch: "And she shall spit in his face" — I might have thought literally on his face? The verse states: "before the eyes of the elders" — spit that is visible to the elders.

Tosafot on Niddah 55b:1:1.hebrew: כי איצטריך קרא למשא - וא"ת: למשא נמי לא איצטריך, מההיא טעמא דלא גרע משכבת זרע, דהא בזב קיימין; ואיכא למ"ד סוף פ"ב דב"ק (דף כה.), שכבת זרע מטמאה במשא אפילו בלא ציחצוחי זיבה מק"ו: ומה טהור בטהור, פירוש רוק, טמא בטמא; טמא בטהור, שכבת זרע, אינו דין שיהא טמא בטמא? ויש לומר: דלא קשה מידי, דאין לנו לעשות זאת הזיבה שהיא גורמת טומאה, דהיינו ראייה שניה, משאם היתה שכבת זרע; וקרי שאחר ראייה ראשונה טהור ממשא, שאינו זב. וה"ק: דלא גרע מאילו היתה ראייה זו שכבת זרע, דמטמא במגע ולא במשא. ומק"ו לא אתי, דאין זה טמא בטמא, דאכתי אינו טמא, אלא על ידי ראייה זו הוא נעשה טמא. וא"ת: כיון דמגע נפקא לן בלא קרא, היכי שייך לומר שעיר המשתלח יוכיח? הא לא דמי, דבזוב איכא טומאת מגע! וכי האי גוונא אמר בפרק כל הבשר (חולין קטו:) גבי בשר בחלב, דיליף איסור אכילה מואנשי קדש תהיון ואיסור הנאה מערלה מק"ו, ופריך: ונילף כולה מילתא מערלה? ומשני: משום דאיכא למימר, חוסם פי פרה ודש בה וחורש בשור וחמור יוכיח, שנעבדה בהן עבירה ומותרין אף באכילה; אבל עכשיו דנפקא לן איסור אכילה מקרא, ליכא למימר תו יוכיח, דלא דמי, דאינהו שרי באכילה. ויש לומר: דשעיר המשתלח נמי, כיון דמטמא אחרים העוסקין בו, אינו טהור גמור, ושייך לטומאת עצמו, והוי כאילו טמא במגע, ודמיא לזוב:
Tosafot on Niddah 55b:1:1.english: When the verse was necessary, [it was] for carrying - And if you say: For carrying as well, [a verse] should not be necessary, for that [same] reason, that it is no worse than semen, for we are dealing with a zav; and there is an opinion at the end of the second chapter of Bava Kamma (25a) that semen [of a zav] transmits impurity by carrying, even without traces of zivah, through an a fortiori argument (kal va-chomer): Just as that which is pure in a pure person — meaning saliva — is impure in an impure person, that which is impure in a pure person — semen — is it not logical that it should be impure in an impure person? And one can say that this is no difficulty at all: for we should not treat this zivah which causes the impurity — that is, the second emission — [more strictly] than if it were semen; and a seminal emission after the first emission is pure from [transmitting impurity by] carrying, as he is not [yet] a zav. And this is what [the Gemara] means: that it is no worse than if this emission were semen, which transmits impurity by contact and not by carrying. And it cannot be derived from a kal va-chomer, for this is not [a case of] "impure in an impure person," as he is not yet impure; rather, it is through this emission that he becomes impure. And if you say: Since [the impurity of] contact is derived for us without a verse, how is it applicable to say [that] the scapegoat shall prove it? For it is not similar, as in [the case of] zivah there is the impurity of contact! And along these lines [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "Kol HaBasar" (Chullin 115b) regarding meat [cooked] in milk, where it derives the prohibition of eating from "And you shall be holy men" (Exodus 22:30), and the prohibition of benefit from orlah through a kal va-chomer, and asks: And let us derive the entire matter from orlah? And it answers: Because one can say [that the cases of] one who muzzles the mouth of a cow and threshes with it, and one who plows with an ox and a donkey [together], shall prove it, for a transgression was committed with them and yet they are permitted even for eating; but now that the prohibition of eating is derived for us from a verse, one can no longer say [that they] shall prove it, for they are not similar, as those are permitted for eating. And one can say that the scapegoat as well, since it transmits impurity to others who are engaged with it, is not completely pure, and [this] is associated with its own impurity; and it is as though it is impure by contact, and [thus] it is similar to zivah.

Tosafot on Niddah 55b:8:1.hebrew: כיחו וניעו - כיחו הוא הבא מכח רב מן החזה, ניעו ע"י נענוע מעט; כך מפרש ר"ת. ויש לפרש נמי איפכא: ניעו שמנענע כל גופו, כיחו בכח מעט. ובמתני', דלא תנא כיחו, לא חש להאריך. אבל תימה: דתנן ניעו מקמי רוק, דעיקר, דכתיב בהדיא! וי"ל, דהך דאתיא מדרשא חביבא ליה:
Tosafot on Niddah 55b:8:1.english: His phlegm and his mucus - Keiḥo [phlegm] is that which comes with great force from the chest, [while] ni'o [mucus] is by means of a slight movement; so explains Rabbeinu Tam. And one can also explain the opposite: ni'o is [when] one shakes his entire body, [while] keiḥo is with slight force. And in the Mishna [above, 54b], which did not teach keiḥo, [the Tanna] was not concerned to elaborate. However, it is puzzling that we learned [in the Mishna] ni'o before saliva, which is the primary [substance], as it is written explicitly [in Scripture]! And one can say that that which is derived from an exposition is beloved to him [and was therefore taught first].
